reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) from a single study on Hf-coated VZrHfNbTa HEA directly supports the formation of a dense HfO2 layer, reduced weight gain, and Zr diffusion bonding, but the substrate is a refractory HEA, not a zirconium alloy, and the coating method is only hot-press sintering, not laser cladding.
premises: Hafnium coating forms a dense, stable HfO2 protective layer during high-temperature oxidation
HfO2 layer limits oxygen ingress and reduces oxidation of the underlying alloy
Coated samples show lower weight gain than uncoated samples
Coating can be applied by hot-press sintering or laser cladding
Zirconium diffusion into the hafnium coating creates a transition layer that bonds coating to substrate
